shortDescription: The South African rand was subdued in early trade on Monday, as investors awaited a raft of economic data this week, including gross domestic product, current account, mining and manufacturing figures, for clues on the health of the economy.

children: The South African rand was subdued in early trade on Monday, as investors awaited a raft of economic data this week, including gross domestic product, current account, mining and manufacturing figures, for clues on the health of the economy.
At 0655 GMT, the rand traded at 15.9675 against the dollar
, little changed from its previous close, with the market largely shrugging off reserves data.
South Africa's net foreign reserves rose to $73.69 billion at the end of August from $71.76 billion in July, central bank data showed on Monday.
Focus will now turn to second-quarter GDP data (ZAGDPY=ECI) due on Tuesday, followed by current account (ZACACT=ECI), mining (ZAMNG=ECI) and manufacturing (ZAMAN=ECI) figures on Thursday.
last traded flat against a basket of currencies despite a ramp-up in U.S. rate-hike bets, as tension in the
heightened inflation risks that could force global central banks to tighten policy in tandem.
South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond (ZAR2035=) weakened slightly in early deals, as the yield rose 1 basis point to 8.53%.
